## HueMux v0.0.2-alpha.16 — Long press does nothing, visibly

> **Alpha.** Everything in alpha.15, plus the long-press fix. Test this one
> instead of alpha.15.

### Holding a control no longer does anything

Resting a finger on a button or a slider tinted it blue, and holding it left
the control in a stuck half-selected state that survived lifting the finger.

Nothing in this app uses a long press. Every control acts on release. So the
gesture is disabled rather than delayed — a 500ms threshold would still end in
a gesture that does nothing.

It turned out to be three separate platform features, and switching one off
leaves the other two:

- the tap highlight (the blue overlay),
- the text selection a long press starts (the stuck state),
- the haptic tick and context menu, which no stylesheet can reach and which the
  app now consumes directly.

Text you might want to copy is unaffected. The diagnostics dump in particular
stays selectable, because hand-selecting it is the fallback for any device
where the download or the clipboard fails.

### From alpha.15, if you skipped it

- **The diagnostics button saves a file again.** It broke in alpha.13 when the
  download was moved into a hidden iframe, where Android's WebView does not
  intercept it. Files no longer travel through a navigation at all: the page
  fetches the text and the app writes it to **Downloads**, then offers
  **Share**.
- **Recordings say where they went**, and can be shared from the sync page.
- **Hash navigation works**, so the Back button after a tab switch does
  something.

### Still unverified

Everything Android-specific, as before — this machine has no Android SDK. That
now includes the long-click suppression, the write to Downloads, and the share
sheet.

If full-resolution recording still fails, alpha.14 added a reason to the
diagnostics report and alpha.15 made the report reachable again. That file is
the thing to send.
